title: Reading Sensor Data
summary: Let's stream live sensor telemetry straight into your computer's screen using the Arduino IDE Serial Monitor!

steps.title: Reading Sensor Data

quickCheck.question: Which command in `setup()` opens the serial data channel so your computer can display sensor telemetry?
quickCheck.explanation: Serial.begin(9600) sets the communication speed (baud rate) and opens the serial channel between the Arduino and computer.
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: From Lesson 4 & 6: Serial.begin(9600) is the handshake that lets your Arduino talk to the Serial Monitor at 9600 bits per second.

quickCheck.question: What happens if the baud rate selected in the Arduino IDE Serial Monitor does not match `Serial.begin()` in your code?
options: The telemetry will appear as garbled symbols, gibberish, or blank lines
The Arduino microcontroller chip will be permanently damaged
The sensor will stop measuring physical values
quickCheck.explanation: When baud rates mismatch, the computer and Arduino sample bits at different speeds, resulting in garbled characters or blank text.
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: Both sides must agree on the exact same speed (like 9600 baud) to understand each other's data signals.

steps.title: The Serial Telemetry Pipeline
steps.markdownContent:
### Streaming Data Over UART Serial

To see what your robot senses, you stream digital telemetry over the USB cable to your computer's screen:

```
[ Sensor Voltage ] ──► [ ATmega328P ADC ]
                              │
                              ▼ (10-bit integer 0-1023)
                       [ Hardware UART ]
                              │
                              ▼ (ASCII text bytes at 9600 bits/sec)
                       [ USB-Serial Bridge Chip ]
                              │
                              ▼ (USB D+ / D- packets)
                       [ Computer Screen: Arduino Serial Monitor ]
```

- `Serial.begin(9600)`: Synchronizes the communication clock to 9,600 baud (bits per second).
- `Serial.print()`: Streams text or numbers side-by-side on the same terminal line.
- `Serial.println()`: Appends a carriage return and newline (`\r\n`), moving the cursor down to the next row.

interactiveConfig.question: What happens if the baud rate selected in the Arduino Serial Monitor does not match Serial.begin() in your sketch?
options: The Serial Monitor displays garbled, unintelligible symbols or question marks
The Arduino board immediately powers off
The sensor values are automatically multiplied by 10
interactiveConfig.explanation: When baud rates do not match, the receiver samples incoming bits at the wrong clock frequency, causing timing framing errors and garbled output.

questions.question: What happens if the baud rate selected in the Arduino Serial Monitor does not match Serial.begin() in your sketch?
options: The Serial Monitor displays garbled, unintelligible symbols or question marks
The Arduino board immediately powers off
The sensor values are automatically multiplied by 10
questions.explanation: When baud rates do not match, the receiver samples incoming bits at the wrong clock frequency, causing timing framing errors and garbled output.

questions.question: What is the key difference between Serial.print("Value") and Serial.println("Value")?
options: Serial.println() automatically moves the terminal cursor to a new line after printing
Serial.println() only prints numbers while Serial.print() only prints letters
Serial.println() sends data directly to an SD card instead of USB
questions.explanation: Serial.println() appends newline and carriage return characters at the end of the text, advancing subsequent output to the next line.
